answer: One defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can influence shared decisions. The protocol caps votes by deposited stake, then confiscates that stake when fraud is proven through an auditable challenge process. Creating a thousand fake identities no longer multiplies influence: the attacker must fund each one, tying up real capital and risking its loss. A canyon of sable and ivory tokens is irrelevant unless they meet the same costly deposit rule.
